## What is Lilys Builder?

Lilys Builder is a developer utility for constructing interactive WhatsApp message payloads without having to manually assemble complex nested objects.

Instead of writing a large payload by hand, you can create a message through a small chain of readable methods:

```js
const Lily = require("lilys-builder");

const message = new Lily.Button()
  .text("Welcome!")
  .button("Menu", "menu")
  .button("Owner", "owner")
  .footer("Lilys Builder")
  .build();
```

The builder is intended for **Baileys-based WhatsApp bots**, especially projects using CommonJS.

## Get Started

### Install

```bash
npm install lilys-builder
```

If Baileys is not already installed in your project:

```bash
npm install lilys-baileys
```

Then load the builder:

```js
const Lily = require("lilys-builder");
```

---

# Message Builders

## 01 — Button

Use `Button` when you need a compact interactive message.

```js
const message = new Lily.Button()
  .text("Select an option")
  .button("Open Menu", "menu")
  .button("Contact Owner", "owner")
  .footer("Powered by Lilys Builder")
  .build();
```

### Available methods

```text
.text(value)
.button(label, id)
.header(value)
.footer(value)
.viewOnce()
.build()
```

---

## 02 — ButtonV2

For layouts containing multiple rows, use `ButtonV2`.

```js
const message = new Lily.ButtonV2()
  .text("Choose one of the options below.")
  .row(row =>
    row
      .button("Menu", "menu")
      .button("Owner", "owner")
  )
  .row(row =>
    row.button("Help", "help")
  )
  .footer("Lilys Builder")
  .build();
```

### Available methods

```text
.text(value)
.row(callback)
.header(value)
.footer(value)
.viewOnce()
.build()
```

---

## 03 — Carousel

Build multiple cards inside one carousel message.

```js
const message = new Lily.Carousel()
  .card(card =>
    card
      .image("https://example.com/image.jpg")
      .title("First Card")
      .text("Card description")
      .button("Open", "open")
  )
  .card(card =>
    card
      .image("https://example.com/image-2.jpg")
      .title("Second Card")
      .text("Another description")
      .button("View", "view")
  )
  .build();
```

### Card API

```text
.image(url)
.title(value)
.text(value)
.button(label, id)
```

### Carousel API

```text
.card(callback)
.build()
```

---

## 04 — AIRich

`AIRich` is intended for messages that require richer text formatting.

```js
const message = new Lily.AIRich()
  .text("Visit [Google](https://google.com) for more information.")
  .build();
```

Configuration methods:

```text
.text(value)
.extract(value)
.hyperlink(value)
.citation(value)
.latex(value)
.build()
```

Example:

```js
const message = new Lily.AIRich()
  .extract(true)
  .hyperlink(true)
  .citation(true)
  .latex(true)
  .text("Your rich response here.")
  .build();
```

---

# Native Flow

Projects that use WhatsApp Native Flow can access the corresponding builder:

```js
const flow = new Lily.NativeFlow();
```

Native Flow payloads depend on the implementation and Baileys version used by the project.

# Integration Example

A simple menu can be prepared like this:

```js
const Lily = require("lilys-builder");

async function createMenu() {
  return new Lily.ButtonV2()
    .text("🌸 Main Menu")
    .row(row =>
      row
        .button("All Menu", "allmenu")
        .button("Owner", "owner")
    )
    .row(row =>
      row.button("Information", "info")
    )
    .footer("Lilys Builder")
    .build();
}
```

The generated payload should be passed to the sending layer used by your Baileys implementation.

# Requirements

Before using the package, make sure your environment provides:

```text
Node.js
Baileys
CommonJS support
```

Recommended project loading style:

```js
const Lily = require("lilys-builder");
```

---

# Project Philosophy

Lilys Builder is built around a straightforward idea:

**Keep message construction readable.**

The API separates message construction into small builder operations so bot source code remains easier to maintain when menus, cards, buttons, or rich responses become more complex.

---

# Updating Your Project

After installing a new package release, refresh the dependency with:

```bash
npm update lilys-builder
```

Or install a specific version:

```bash
npm install lilys-builder@VERSION
```

Check the installed version:

```bash
npm list lilys-builder
```

---

# Troubleshooting

### Package cannot be loaded

Check the installation:

```bash
npm install lilys-builder
```

Then verify:

```bash
npm list lilys-builder
```

### Baileys dependency error

Make sure the required Baileys package is installed and that its version is compatible with the builder release.

```bash
npm install @whiskeysockets/baileys
```

### Message payload does not work

Inspect the generated payload and verify that the Baileys version currently used by your bot supports the message type being generated.
